PURPOSE: The Present Level of Educational Performance describes the effects of the student's disability upon the student's involvement and progress in the general curriculum and area(s) of need.
[student] continues to struggle with following staff requests or directions.
[student] will almost always say "no" or shake his head to communicate that he does not want or will not do what staff is asking.
After [student]'s initial refusal to comply, he complies with staff 5/10 opportunities.
[student] has been doing a good job of handling frustration and conflict without aggression.
[student] comes to staff and asks for help when he is having a conflict with a peer.
On two occasions this school year, [student] has pushed a chair over in frustration.
On both occasions, [student] eventually picked the chair up and apologized for his behavior.
[student] is currently resolving conflict without aggression 9/10 opportunities.
[student] has been very reluctant to participate in group academic activities.
He prefers working independently with staff support.
At this time, [student] participates in group classroom activities 3/10 opportunities.
[student] is completing a 6.0 grade math curriculum this year.
He has demonstrated he can use a calculator to solve 6.0 calculation problems accurately 8/10 opportunities.
Fluency has not been an issue and the IEP team recommends dropping this measurable skill.
[student] has been independently completing 6.0 grade level word problems accurately 5/10 opportunities.
[student] lacks some confidence and often asks for help when he could have solved problems independently.
With minimal help, [student] is often able to ask questions to confirm his thinking, and then goes on to accurately solve the problem.
[student] has been very reluctant to read silently or aloud this school year.
For a time, [student] was reading 1:1 with staff in an alternative location.
This intervention worked well for 2 months.
Then, [student] demanded staff do most of the reading aloud while he listened.
At this time, [student] takes part in whole group reading, but he refuses to read aloud and rarely follows along reading the book while others read aloud.
[student] is currently reading 60 WCPM at the 6.0 grade level.
[student] is able to answer comprehension questions at the 6.0 grade level 75% of the time.
When completing daily reading logs, [student] is able to write sentences using correct punctuation and capitalization 80% of the time.
When asked to write a paragraph response for his scrapbook or other English assignments, [student] most often refuses to complete the assignment.
[student] does best with 1:1 support, but often tries to get the staff to do all the work.
At this time, [student] writes correct sentences to complete a paragraph with proper content and pragmatics 50% of the time.
[student] continues to struggle with completing assignments.
When [student] is willing to complete an assignment, he always works hard and does a good job.
The IEP team has observed [student] is very concerned about making mistakes on assignments.
He may be refusing to complete some assignments because he is feeling anxious about making a mistake.
At this time, [student] independently completes assignments 3/10 opportunities.

PURPOSE: IEPs must include a statement of measurable annual goals, including academic and functional goals.

By 01/11/2013, when given 7.0 calculation problems, [student] will calculate problems using a calculator improving accuracy from 80% at the 6.0 grade level to 80% at the 7.0 grade level as measured by classroom assessments.

By 01/11/2013, when given 7.0 grade level word problems, [student] will independently solve the problem improving accuracy from 50% at the 6.0 grade level to 80% at the 7.0 grade level as measured by classroom assessments.

By 01/11/2013, when given 6.0 grade level text, [student] will read aloud or silently improving fluency from 60 correct words per minute to 100 correct words per minute as measured by classroom assessments.

By 01/11/2013, when given 7.0 grade level text, [student] will answer comprehension questions improving accuracy from 75% at the 6.0 grade level to 80% at the 7.0 grade level as measured by classroom assessments.
By 01/11/2013, when given a direction from staff, [student] will comply improving success from 50% to 80% of the time as measured by classroom data.
By 01/11/2013, when given a situation that is frustrating, [student] will resolve his feelings without aggression improving success from 90% to 100% of the time as measured by classroom data.

By 01/11/2013, when given an opportunity to participate in group academic activities, [student] will appropriately work with staff and peers improving success from 30% to 80% of the time as measured by classroom data.
By 01/11/2013, when given an academic assignment, [student] will complete the assignment improving success from 30% to 80% of the time as measured by classroom data.

By 01/11/2013, when given a writing prompt, [student] will write a paragraph with sentences that have correct content and pragmatics improving accuracy from 50% to 90% of the time as measured by classroom assessments.

By 01/11/2013, when given a daily reading log to complete, [student] will write sentences using correct punctuation and capitalization improving accuracy from 80% to 95% of the time as measured by classroom assessments.
